proofs.proof_tex:
On the fork generic locus, vertex \(1\) is the only source. By the covariance-branch lemma, \(D_1\) has its unique regular factor line, whereas each of \(D_2,D_3,D_4\) has rank two and has exactly two real factor lines. Hence the regular factorization has exactly
\[
 1\cdot 2^3=8
\]
line branches. The rational projective gauge in the factor-branch definition fixes the scale on every selected line, so no additional scaling branch remains.

The exceptional polynomials used here are not identically zero. Indeed, substitution of the worked true point with \(T=2\) into the covariance-difference formula of \(\mathrm{lem:covariance\text{-}branches}\) gives the following unnormalized factor choices:
\[
 \ell_1=(1,2)^{\mathsf T},\qquad
 \ell_2\in\{(2,3)^{\mathsf T},(5,8)^{\mathsf T}\},\qquad
 \ell_3\in\{(7,11)^{\mathsf T},(87/2,139/2)^{\mathsf T}\},
\]
and
\[
 \ell_4\in\{(4,7)^{\mathsf T},(13,45/2)^{\mathsf T}\}.
\]
For the four choices of \((\ell_2,\ell_3)\), direct expansion of the determinant of the first three columns of \(B_{\ell}\) gives, respectively,
\[
 3,\qquad \frac{595}{4},\qquad -6,\qquad -\frac{35}{2}.
\]
These values do not depend on the choice of \(\ell_4\). The endpoint determinants are
\[
 \det[\ell_1,\ell_2]\in\{-1,-2\},\qquad
 \det[\ell_3,\ell_4]
 \in\left\{5,\frac{29}{2},\frac{53}{2},\frac{301}{4}\right\}.
\]
Thus every displayed value is nonzero. Each relevant minor is therefore a nonzero polynomial in the true parameters. By the definitions of \(\mathcal Q_{\mathrm{fork}}\) and \(\mathcal M^{\circ}_{\mathrm{fork},2,4}\), the selected chart denominators and these rank minors do not vanish on the stated generic locus.

Fix one of the eight branches. Because \(p=2\), equality of the three distinct entries of the baseline covariance is exactly
\[
 B_{\ell}v'=\operatorname{vech}(\Sigma^{(0)}),\qquad
 B_{\ell}
 =\left[
   (\ell_{k1}^{2},\ell_{k1}\ell_{k2},\ell_{k2}^{2})^{\mathsf T}
  \right]_{k=1}^{4}.
\]
The preceding nonvanishing minor and the fact that \(B_{\ell}\) has three rows imply
\[
 \operatorname{rank}B_{\ell}=3.
\]
Consequently the displayed linear map is onto \(\mathbb R^3\), and its complete solution set is the affine line
\[
 v'=v'_0+s n,\qquad n\in\ker B_{\ell}\setminus\{0\}.
\]
Candidate baseline positivity is exactly the four inequalities \(v'_i>0\). In particular, every division by a component of \(v'\) below is justified on the legal region.

The nonzero determinant \(\det[\ell_1,\ell_2]\) makes \((\ell_1,\ell_2)\) a basis of \(\mathbb R^2\). There are therefore unique scalars \(\zeta,\rho_2\) satisfying
\[
 m_2=\zeta\ell_1+\rho_2\ell_2.
\]
For the candidate graph, vertex \(2\) has the sole ancestor and parent \(1\). Thus the branch equation \(Lz_2+\rho_2\ell_2=m_2\) forces
\[
 z_2=(\zeta,0,0,0)^{\mathsf T}.
\]
Since \(z_2=\operatorname{diag}(v')h'_2\), it follows that
\[
 h'_2=(\zeta/v'_1,0,0,0),\qquad
 t'_2=v'_2+2\rho_2-\frac{\zeta^2}{v'_1}.
\]
The exact-change condition is \(\zeta\ne0\), intervention-variance positivity is \(t'_2>0\), and if \(x=\Lambda'^{(0)}_{21}\), retention of the edge \(1\to2\) is
\[
 x+\frac{\zeta}{v'_1}\ne0.
\]

For \(k\in\{3,4\}\), the candidate graph gives \(\operatorname{pa}_{G'_{\mathrm{fork}}}(k)=\{2\}\) and \(\operatorname{an}_{G'_{\mathrm{fork}}}(k)=\{1,2\}\). Write a possible actual row as \(h'_k=(r_1,r_2,0,0)\). Multiplication by \(U=I_4-\Lambda'^{(0)}\) gives
\[
 \delta'_{k1}=r_1-xr_2,\qquad \delta'_{k2}=r_2.
\]
Exact support \(\operatorname{supp}(\delta'_k)=\{2\}\) is therefore equivalent to
\[
 h'_k=\beta_k(x,1,0,0),\qquad \beta_k\ne0.
\]
It follows from \(z_k=\operatorname{diag}(v')h'_k\) that
\[
 z_k=\beta_k(v'_1x,v'_2,0,0)^{\mathsf T},\qquad
 Lz_k=\beta_k g,\qquad
 g=v'_1x\ell_1+v'_2\ell_2.
\]
The factor equation becomes
\[
 m_k-\beta_kg=\rho_k\ell_k.
\]
Taking determinants with \(\ell_k\) gives
\[
 \det[m_k,\ell_k]-\beta_k\det[g,\ell_k]=0.
\]
Since \(D_k=\ell_km_k^{\mathsf T}+m_k\ell_k^{\mathsf T}\) has rank two, the vectors \(\ell_k,m_k\) are independent, and hence \(\det[m_k,\ell_k]\ne0\). A feasible solution therefore cannot have \(\det[g,\ell_k]=0\), and division yields
\[
 \beta_k=\frac{\det[m_k,\ell_k]}{\det[g,\ell_k]}.
\]
Substitution in the variance identity from the complete covariance branch gives
\[
 t'_k
 =v'_k+2\rho_k-\sum_{i=1}^{4}\frac{z_{ki}^{2}}{v'_i}
 =v'_k+2\rho_k-\beta_k^2(v'_1x^2+v'_2),
\]
and legality is exactly \(t'_k>0\). No argument divides by \(t'_k-v'_k\), so the equality \(t'_k=v'_k\) remains admissible. At the source \(1\), one has \(h'_1=z_1=0\), \(m_1=\rho_1\ell_1\), and \(t'_1=v'_1+2\rho_1>0\), as required by the inherited branch constraints.

It remains to recover the baseline structural mixing. Put
\[
 b=\Lambda'^{(0)}_{32},\qquad c=\Lambda'^{(0)}_{42}.
\]
Then
\[
 F'=LU
 =\bigl[\ell_1-x\ell_2,\ \ell_2-b\ell_3-c\ell_4,\ \ell_3,\ \ell_4\bigr].
\]
The explicit branch inequations require the first, third, and fourth columns here to be nonzero and pairwise noncollinear. Because \(\det[\ell_3,\ell_4]\ne0\), the affine map
\[
 (b,c)\longmapsto\ell_2-b\ell_3-c\ell_4
\]
is onto \(\mathbb R^2\). Requiring its image to be nonzero and not collinear with any of the other three columns excludes only finitely many proper affine subsets of the \((b,c)\)-plane. The conditions
\[
 b\ne0,\qquad c\ne0,\qquad b+\beta_3\ne0,\qquad c+\beta_4\ne0
\]
exclude four additional proper affine lines and express exact baseline support and retained edges. A finite union of proper affine lines and points cannot cover \(\mathbb R^2\), so legal \(b,c\) exist.

Necessity of all displayed equations and inequations follows from \(\mathrm{lem:covariance\text{-}branches}\). Conversely, start with a solution of one of the eight systems, choose \(b,c\) outside the preceding finite forbidden union, set \(F'=LU\), and set \(\delta'_k{}^{\mathsf T}=h'_k{}^{\mathsf T}U\). The baseline equation gives
\[
 \Sigma'^{(0)}=L\operatorname{diag}(v')L^{\mathsf T}=\Sigma^{(0)}.
\]
For every \(k\), write \(z_k=\operatorname{diag}(v')h'_k\). The constructed identities imply
\[
 m_k=Lz_k+\rho_k\ell_k,\qquad
 h'_k{}^{\mathsf T}\operatorname{diag}(v')h'_k+t'_k-v'_k=2\rho_k.
\]
Applying the covariance-difference identity to the candidate therefore gives
\[
\begin{aligned}
 D'_k
 &=\ell_k(Lz_k)^{\mathsf T}+(Lz_k)\ell_k^{\mathsf T}
   +2\rho_k\ell_k\ell_k^{\mathsf T}\\
 &=\ell_km_k^{\mathsf T}+m_k\ell_k^{\mathsf T}
 =D_k.
\end{aligned}
\]
Together with the baseline equality, this proves \(\Sigma'^{(k)}=\Sigma^{(k)}\) for all five contexts \(k\in K\). Thus every legal twin enters one of the eight systems, and every legal solution reconstructs a twin satisfying the original covariance equations. Finally, \(\mathrm{prop:fork\text{-}rational\text{-}collision}\) supplies such a legal twin for every \(T>0\), \(T\ne1\), so completeness places each worked point on one of the eight systems. This proves exactly the asserted regular two-scalar reduction and no chamberwise density conclusion.

Let \(G,G'\) satisfy the displayed assumptions. The value of \(\omega_p(G,G')\) is not needed for either established reduction. First, \(\mathrm{thm:terminal\text{-}certificate}\) is sound and complete for the actual-row class and gives the stated \(O(q^5)\) rational-function field-operation bound.

Second, fix \(\theta\in\mathcal M^{\circ}_{\mathrm{branch},p,q}(G,G')\). By \(\mathrm{lem:covariance\text{-}branches}\), every legal positive-real covariance twin chooses the unique factor line at each of the \(r\) sources and one of two factor lines at each of the \(q-r\) nonsources. Thus it determines one of at most
\[
 2^{q-r}
\]
systems in \(\mathfrak B_p(G,G')\). The converse part of that lemma reconstructs a legal twin from every solution of any such system, including all exact-support, retained-edge, mixing, sign, and positive-variance conditions. Quantifying \(\theta\) and projecting away the candidate variables therefore represents the regular covariance fiber exactly as the union of those projected systems.

For \(p=2\) and the fork pair, \(\mathrm{thm:fork\text{-}eight\text{-}branch\text{-}classification}\) reduces each system to \((s,x)\), and \(\mathrm{thm:fork\text{-}all\text{-}chamber\text{-}projection}\) proves the exact union identity and the chamberwise density condition that remains to be decided. That theorem also proves that the worked rational family and its local regular neighborhoods do not decide the density alternative. None of the invoked results specifies bag transition rules, bounds elimination fill-in, constructs a dense cover or separator for the projected union, or derives the former bit and coefficient exponents. The conclusions proved above are therefore exactly the two stated reductions; the stronger compiler, complexity, and pathwidth claims are not conclusions of this theorem.

added_lemmas.statement:
For \(p=2\) and the pair \((G_{\mathrm{fork}},G'_{\mathrm{fork}})\), index the eight systems of \(\mathfrak B_2(G_{\mathrm{fork}},G'_{\mathrm{fork}})\) by \(\eta\in\{0,1\}^3\). For every full-dimensional connected chamber \(C\) of \(\mathcal M^{\circ}_{\mathrm{fork},2,4}(G_{\mathrm{fork}},G'_{\mathrm{fork}})\), let \(\mathscr S_{\eta,C}\subseteq C\times\mathbb R^2\) consist of the triples \((\theta,s,x)\) satisfying all baseline-variance, intervention-variance, denominator, exact-support, retained-edge, mixing, and exceptional-polynomial equations and inequations of branch \(\eta\), with the reconstructed \(\theta'\in\mathcal M_{2,4}(G'_{\mathrm{fork}})\) required to satisfy \(\Sigma_{\theta'}^{(k)}=\Sigma_{\theta}^{(k)}\) for every \(k\in K\). If \(\pi_C(\theta,s,x)=\theta\), then
\[
 \mathcal E_2(G_{\mathrm{fork}},G'_{\mathrm{fork}})\cap C
 =\bigcup_{\eta\in\{0,1\}^3}\pi_C(\mathscr S_{\eta,C}).
\]
Since \(G'_{\mathrm{fork}}\notin\mathsf H_{\mathrm{soft}}(G_{\mathrm{fork}})\), membership in \(\mathsf{Frontier}_2(G_{\mathrm{fork}})\) is equivalent to the condition that, for every such \(C\),
\[
 \operatorname{relint}_C\!\left(
 C\setminus\operatorname{cl}_C
 \left(\bigcup_{\eta\in\{0,1\}^3}\pi_C(\mathscr S_{\eta,C})\right)
 \right)=\varnothing.
\]
Let \(\theta_{\mathrm{true}}(T)\) denote the true-coordinate projection of the pair \(\mathcal W_{\mathrm{fork}}(T)\). This one-parameter family, even together with regular open neighborhoods of all its audited points, is insufficient to decide the density condition: there are relatively semialgebraic subsets of a full-dimensional chamber containing the same true-coordinate family and neighborhoods but having opposite answers to the displayed density test. Thus the eight-branch reduction gives an exact projection problem, but neither a chamberwise dense cover nor a full-dimensional separator follows without an additional global projection argument.
added_lemmas.proof_tex:
Fix a full-dimensional connected chamber \(C\) and a true point \(\theta\in C\). If \(\theta\in\mathcal E_2(G_{\mathrm{fork}},G'_{\mathrm{fork}})\), the definition of the covariance fiber supplies a legal candidate \(\theta'\in\mathcal M_{2,4}(G'_{\mathrm{fork}})\) satisfying
\[
 \Sigma_{\theta'}^{(k)}=\Sigma_{\theta}^{(k)}\qquad(k\in K).
\]
The complete direction of \(\mathrm{thm:fork\text{-}eight\text{-}branch\text{-}classification}\) assigns this candidate to one of the eight factor-line choices and produces scalars \((s,x)\) satisfying every equation and inequation in that branch. Hence \((\theta,s,x)\in\mathscr S_{\eta,C}\) for some \(\eta\), and
\[
 \theta\in\bigcup_{\eta}\pi_C(\mathscr S_{\eta,C}).
\]
Conversely, if \((\theta,s,x)\in\mathscr S_{\eta,C}\), the soundness direction of the same theorem reconstructs all remaining candidate coefficients and positive variances. Its final covariance calculation verifies the original equations in every context, so the reconstructed point belongs to \(\mathcal M_{2,4}(G'_{\mathrm{fork}})\) and is a witness that \(\theta\in\mathcal E_2(G_{\mathrm{fork}},G'_{\mathrm{fork}})\). This proves the set equality.

By \(\mathrm{prop:fork\text{-}rational\text{-}collision}\), the candidate fork is not in \(\mathsf H_{\mathrm{soft}}(G_{\mathrm{fork}})\). It remains to relate the fork locus to the branch locus used in the definition of \(\mathsf{Cov}_2\). By construction, the fork locus removes from the branch locus only the zero sets of finitely many nonzero exceptional polynomials. Each such zero set has empty relative interior in every full-dimensional branch chamber. Hence the fork locus is relatively dense there, and its full-dimensional connected chambers form a relatively open dense refinement. A subset is dense in the original branch chamber if and only if its intersection is dense in every chamber of this refinement: the forward implication follows by restricting a dense set to a relatively open subset, and the reverse implication follows because the union of the refined chambers is dense. Substituting the proved set equality into the definition of \(\mathsf{Cov}_2(G_{\mathrm{fork}})\) therefore gives
\[
 G'_{\mathrm{fork}}\in\mathsf{Frontier}_2(G_{\mathrm{fork}})
 \quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
 \operatorname{relint}_C\!\left(
 C\setminus\operatorname{cl}_C
 \left(\bigcup_{\eta}\pi_C(\mathscr S_{\eta,C})\right)
 \right)=\varnothing
\]
for every full-dimensional \(C\), which is the asserted equivalence.

It remains to determine exactly what the worked family proves about this equivalence. Its true coordinates satisfy fixed affine equations, including \(v_1=v_2=v_3=v_4=1\) and the displayed fixed baseline structural coefficients and loading matrix. Therefore its image is contained in a proper affine algebraic subset \(Z\) of the full-dimensional true parameter domain. Let \(C\) be any full-dimensional chamber meeting the family. Since \(C\) is full-dimensional, \(C\setminus Z\ne\varnothing\); choose \(\theta_0\in C\setminus Z\). As \(Z\) is closed, there is a sufficiently small relative open ball \(B\subset C\) about \(\theta_0\) whose closure is disjoint from \(Z\). Define
\[
 P_0=C\setminus\overline B,\qquad P_1=C.
\]
Both sets are relatively semialgebraic, both contain every \(\theta_{\mathrm{true}}(T)\in C\), and both contain a relative neighborhood in \(C\) of every such point. Nevertheless,
\[
 \operatorname{relint}_C(C\setminus\operatorname{cl}_C P_0)\supseteq B\ne\varnothing,
 \qquad
 \operatorname{relint}_C(C\setminus\operatorname{cl}_C P_1)=\varnothing.
\]
Thus inclusion of the rational family and local regular realizability are logically compatible with both possible global density outcomes. The actual projected union is fixed by the eight systems, but deciding which outcome it has requires information about that union away from the audited family. This proves the stated insufficiency and isolates the missing global projection argument.
added_lemmas.justification: This theorem turns the directive's early-kill test into the exact eight-branch projection identity and proves why the audited rational family and local regularity cannot settle the required chamberwise density alternative.
added_lemmas.gap: The exact projected union is identified, but no global elimination invariant, relatively dense cover, or full-dimensional separator is available without solving the positive-real projection over all true parameters.
added_lemmas.consumer: The companion workflow may enumerate and verify fork covariance twins, but it must not claim that higher cumulants remove, or fail to remove, all covariance alternatives until the displayed chamberwise density condition is certified.

prose_updates.tldr: Actual soft-intervention rows \(h_k^{\mathsf T}=\delta_k^{\mathsf T}(I_q-\Lambda^{(0)})^{-1}\) admit the proved terminal-copy and affine-support compatibility test. In the noninjective regime \(2\le p<q\), regular covariance twins are exactly a finite union of positive-real factor-line projections. For the \(p=2,q=4\) fork, all eight branches reduce losslessly to two candidate scalars and reconstruct the original five covariance equations; the positive rational \(T\)-family is valid but supplies only local realizations. The required all-chamber projection classification is not proved, so the bounded-width realization-or-separator compiler and its complexity headline are retracted. The prospective LCD workflow can report the corrected actual-row class and enumerate covariance alternatives, but it cannot yet certify whether higher cumulants remove all covariance alternatives.

project_justification.gap: Problem 5.2 of Leyes Carreno, Meroni, and Seigal asks whether covariance and higher-cumulant information distinguish compatible graph classes. After correcting Definition 3.14 to use actual intervention rows, the noninjective covariance question becomes density of a union of positive-real projected branches in every full-dimensional sign-and-variance chamber. Existing linkage, positive-semidefinite realization, half-trek, and generic real-elimination results do not supply the required graph-specific non-quantifier-elimination density certificate.
project_justification.niche: The proved contribution isolates the exact obstruction. Terminal compatibility has finite linkage and affine certificates, while every regular covariance twin belongs to one of at most \(2^{q-r}\) factor-line systems. The four-node fork is reduced exactly to eight bivariate systems, including all positivity, denominator, support, retention, mixing, and covariance equations. What remains is global projection geometry over all true parameters, not another local witness.
project_justification.fill: The paper delivers the corrected terminal algorithm, the exact covariance-branch reduction, the complete regular two-scalar fork reduction, and a positive rational covariance collision verified in all five contexts. It also proves that the rational family and local regularity cannot decide chamberwise density. Because the fork projection gate remains unresolved, no bounded-width compiler, certificate-height bound, pathwidth guarantee, all-graph criterion, or generic strictness family is claimed.

prose_updates.related_work: Leyes Carreno, Meroni, and Seigal (2025) derive the actual intervention-row system in Equation (20), use the observational inverse-path class in Definition 3.14, state recovery through Theorem 1.7, and pose graph and covariance questions in Problems 5.1--5.2. The terminal-copy result repairs the mismatch between the actual rows and the observational-path substitution. Squires, Seigal, Bhate, and Uhler (2023) recover transitive-closure information for injective soft-intervention models; their injective result does not decide the noninjective positive-real covariance projection considered here. Half-trek, semidefinite realization, affine-birational transfer, and tree-accelerated quantifier-elimination work remain methodological context. In particular, no complexity comparison is claimed for the retracted covariance-terminal-width compiler, because no theorem translates its proposed frontier state into a projection-complete elimination invariant.
prose_updates.interpretation: The corrected compatible graph set is operational at population level once the aligned factor rows are available. Covariance-only alternatives are also represented exactly by finite branch systems, so any displayed candidate can be checked against every context covariance. However, the existence of the worked fork collision does not establish generic covariance surplus, and failure of selected branches does not establish equality. Until the full chamberwise projected union is certified, the LCD consumer must report this distinction as unresolved rather than asserting that higher cumulants genuinely remove covariance alternatives.
prose_updates.technical_internal_limitation: Exact symbolic verification confirms all five covariance equalities for the rational fork family, positivity of the candidate variances \(T+144/121\) and \(19/4\), the actual-row obstruction, and rank-three regularity of all eight loading choices at audited points. The proof also reconstructs every legal solution of the eight systems back into the original covariance equations. These facts do not classify the union's projection over a full true chamber. The proposed bounded-width definitions do not specify a gluing invariant, prevent elimination fill-in beyond a bag, or derive the advertised bit and coefficient bounds; using unrestricted real quantifier elimination would violate the requested structural criterion.
prose_updates.honest_scope: All covariance-frontier claims remain in the noninjective regime \(2\le p<q\), on the declared theorem-specific generic loci and full-dimensional sign-and-variance chambers. Candidate twins may be variance-neutral, both signs of each true variance change are retained, and no pointwise claim is made on excluded true neutral hyperplanes. The terminal actual-row theorem is exact and independent of variance activity. The fork theorem is a sound-and-complete regular reduction to eight bivariate systems, not an all-chamber feasibility classification. The rational \(T\)-family proves a positive covariance collision and local robustness only. The bounded-width compiler, realization-or-separator output, bit complexity, coefficient growth, pathwidth implication, all-graph positive-real criterion, and infinite generic-strictness families are not established. The prospective workflow may output corrected terminal compatibility and verified individual covariance twins, but not a global high-cumulant information-frontier verdict.
